plans.title: Clear the queue that never got a first reply
plans.problem: 47 conversations have been open for more than 24 hours without a single human reply. To the customer who wrote in, Quasi simply did not answer — and this is the queue that later turns into refund requests and a good share of the 'product not received' chargebacks.
plans.why_it_matters: It is the only target in the red this period: 47 against a ceiling of 20. Every day stuck here becomes a refund or a dispute with the bank later.
plans.metric: Open 24h+ with no reply at or below 20 at week close, three weeks running.

actions.text: Sweep twice a day, 9am and 4pm, through everything past 18 hours without a reply — before it becomes a 24-hour case.
Commslayer rule that pushes any conversation without a human reply for 16 hours to the top of the queue.
Redistribute the Sunday queue — three people currently cover the day with the biggest pile-up.
First-touch macro for tracking questions that answers without needing to pull up the order.

plans.title: Cut tracking volume at the source
plans.problem: One in four contacts is 'where is my order'. These are conversations that should not exist: the customer writes because the shipping email never arrived, or because the tracking number has not moved in days and they conclude the order is lost.
plans.why_it_matters: It is the single largest block of volume in the operation. Bringing it down frees capacity for everything stuck in plan 1, without hiring anyone.
plans.metric: 'Where is my order' drops from 26% to 18% or less of total volume.

actions.text: Proactive email on day 7 post-purchase when tracking has had no new event in 72 hours.
Tracking page on the store itself, instead of sending the customer to the carrier's site.
Real delivery estimate by region on the product page — today it says '5 to 9 days' to everyone.
Review the gap between 'order paid' and 'shipped' with the supplier, currently 3.4 days.

plans.title: Skin reactions need their own protocol
plans.problem: Skin reaction is the reason the team answers fastest and the second slowest to close. The first reply goes out in a little over an hour, but the case stays open because nobody knows when to end it: there is no defined follow-up and no clarity on when to point someone toward medical advice.
plans.why_it_matters: It is the only reason carrying brand and regulatory risk. One badly handled case costs far more than any refund on this list.
plans.metric: Median resolution for 'Skin reaction' at or below 24h, and 100% of cases with a follow-up logged within 72h.

actions.text: Three-question triage script, signed off before it reaches the team.
Refunds up to $90 released without escalation whenever a reaction is reported.
Automatic 72-hour follow-up to confirm the reaction has cleared.
Log the product batch on every case, so it can be cross-checked with the supplier.

plans.title: Subscriptions charging after cancellation
plans.problem: Customers cancel their subscription and get charged on the following cycle. When that happens, a good share of them never write to support — they open a dispute with their bank directly. 'Subscription not cancelled' is now the third most common chargeback reason.
plans.why_it_matters: A subscription chargeback is the worst kind: the fee is charged even when the case is won, and the volume counts toward the card networks' monitoring programmes.
plans.metric: Chargeback rate at or below 0.5% of orders, and zero disputes citing 'subscription not cancelled'.

actions.text: Reproduce the bug: cancelling within 24 hours of billing does not stop the cycle.
Cancellation confirmation email stating the date charges stop.
Visible cancel button in the account, with no need to talk to support.
Blocked: depends on the subscription app migration, no date set.

plans.title: Deliveries lost on the last mile
plans.problem: 'Delivery problem' is the reason that takes longest to close — the case sits waiting on the carrier, which takes days to respond. A share of them come back marked as delivered when the customer never received anything.
plans.why_it_matters: On its own it drags the whole operation's median resolution up, and it is the origin of most replacements shipped.
plans.metric: Median resolution for 'Delivery problem' at or below 40h.

actions.text: Fixed response deadline with the carrier for lost-package investigations.
Reship without waiting for the verdict when the order is worth less than the cost of investigating.
Compare 'delivered but not received' rates by region and cut the worst routes.
